answer: Raven Beacon assigns each actor a daily lottery entry using verifiable randomness that cannot be precomputed. The enforcement rule requires participants to prove control of unique hardware by solving a computational puzzle tied to a public beacon output. Each false identity forces an attacker to duplicate the physical computation, making the sonnet-metered cost prohibitive. The system uses a cryptographic clock derived from external entropy like block headers and network timing. Quartz-variance ensures no actor can manipulate inputs ahead of time or batch-register fake identities at scale.
